theorems.name: Bond Portfolio Second-Order Immunization
theorems.description: Matching the convexity-times-value Σᵢ wᵢ(Tᵢ − t)²·e^{−r(Tᵢ − t)} of the asset and liability bond portfolios gives ∂²(A − L)/∂r² = 0 at the current rate r: the surplus has zero second rate-derivative. theorems.name: Vasicek Terminal Distribution is Gaussian (Wiener Representation)
theorems.description: The Vasicek short-rate SDE dr = κ(θ − r)dt + σ dB has the textbook solution r_T = r₀e^{−κT} + θ(1 − e^{−κT}) + σ ∫₀ᵀ e^{−κ(T−s)} dB_s (cited, not proved here). For κ > 0 and r_T in this Wiener representation, this theorem DERIVES (no longer posits) the terminal law r_T ~ N(vasicekSDEMean, vasicekSDEVariance) = N(r₀e^{−κT}+θ(1−e^{−κT}), σ²(1−e^{−2κT})/(2κ)). The stochastic term is the Wiener integral of the DETERMINISTIC integrand e^{−κ(T−s)}, hence Gaussian (sc-wiener-integral-gaussian) with variance its squared L²-norm ∫₀ᵀ e^{−2κ(T−s)} ds = (1−e^{−2κT})/(2κ) (an FTC computation); the affine map x ↦ mean + σx then sends N(0, ∫kernel²) to N(mean, σ²·∫kernel²) = N(vasicekSDEMean, vasicekSDEVariance) via gaussianReal_const_mul / gaussianReal_const_add. This is the FIRST consumer of the deterministic-integrand Itô tower in the FixedIncome layer — the analytic Wiener/Itô machinery made load-bearing in a pricing module, closing the two-tower gap for the Vasicek short rate (VasicekSDE.lean previously stated this law without derivation).

open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ)
    (r₀ θ σ : ℝ) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    HasLaw (fun ω => vasicekSDEMean r₀ θ κ (T : ℝ)
        + σ * (wienerIntegralLp B hB T (vasicekKernelLp κ hκ.le T) ω))
      (gaussianReal (vasicekSDEMean r₀ θ κ (T : ℝ))
        (vasicekSDEVariance σ κ (T : ℝ)).toNNReal) μ :=
  MathFin.vasicekShortRate_hasLaw_gaussian hB r₀ θ σ hκ T

theorems.name: Vasicek Zero-Coupon Bond Price (Affine Term Structure)
theorems.description: The Vasicek zero-coupon bond price P(0,T) = E[exp(-∫₀ᵀ r_s ds)], the expectation taken under the probability measure that carries the Brownian driver (read as the pricing measure; no change of measure is built in this entry. When μ is instead the real-world measure with a constant market price of risk λ, mf-vasicek-girsanov-bond-price shows that the bond price under the constructed Girsanov measure Q_λ is this same formula at the level θ − λσ/κ). Under Vasicek the integrated short rate ∫₀ᵀ r_s ds = M(T) + σ∫₀ᵀ g dB is again Gaussian (integrated OU kernel g(u) = (1-e^{-κ(T-u)})/κ), so the bond price is a Gaussian Laplace transform and collapses to the classical AFFINE TERM STRUCTURE P(0,T) = A(T)·exp(-B(T)·r₀) with B(T) = (1-e^{-κT})/κ. The exponential-affine dependence on the initial short rate r₀ is the defining property of an affine term-structure model.

import MathFin.FixedIncome.VasicekBondPrice

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

/-- **Vasicek zero-coupon bond price — the affine term structure.**
The expectation `P(0,T) = 𝔼[exp(−∫₀ᵀ r_s ds)]` under the measure carrying `B` (read as the pricing measure) of one unit paid
at `T` under the Vasicek short-rate model separates the initial rate into the
exponential-affine form `P(0,T) = A(T)·exp(−B(T)·r₀)`, `B(T) = (1−e^{−κT})/κ`.
Re-exports `MathFin.vasicekBondPrice_affine`. -/
theorem vasicek_bond_price_affine
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ)
    (r₀ θ σ : ℝ) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (-(vasicekIntegratedRate hB r₀ θ σ hκ T ω)) ∂μ
      = vasicekBondA θ σ κ (T : ℝ) * Real.exp (-(vasicekBondB κ (T : ℝ) * r₀)) :=
  MathFin.vasicekBondPrice_affine hB r₀ θ σ hκ T

theorems.name: CIR Affine Loading B(T) Solves the Riccati Equation
theorems.description: For the Cox–Ingersoll–Ross short rate dr = κ(θ − r)dt + σ√r dW, in the affine form P(0,T) = exp(A(T) − B(T)·r₀) of its bond price, the closed-form rate loading B(T) = 2(e^{γT} − 1)/((γ + κ)(e^{γT} − 1) + 2γ), γ = √(κ² + 2σ²), solves the Riccati equation B'(T) = 1 − κB(T) − ½σ²B(T)² with B(0) = 0, at every real T, whenever κ² + 2σ² > 0. Only this equation is verified: the bond price itself is not derived.

open MathFin

/-- **The CIR rate loading solves the Riccati equation.** With `γ = √(κ² + 2σ²)`, the closed
form `B(T) = 2(e^{γT} − 1) / ((γ + κ)(e^{γT} − 1) + 2γ)` of the CIR affine bond price
`P(0,T) = exp(A(T) − B(T)·r₀)` satisfies `B(0) = 0` and `B'(T) = 1 − κB(T) − ½σ²B(T)²` at every
`T`, whenever `κ² + 2σ² > 0`. Re-exports `MathFin.cirBondB_zero` and
`MathFin.hasDerivAt_cirBondB`. -/

    cirBondB κ σ 0 = 0 ∧
      ∀ T : ℝ, HasDerivAt (cirBondB κ σ)
        (1 - κ * cirBondB κ σ T - σ ^ 2 / 2 * cirBondB κ σ T ^ 2) T :=
  ⟨cirBondB_zero κ σ, hasDerivAt_cirBondB h⟩

theorems.name: Forward Price under the T-Forward Measure
theorems.description: The T-forward measure Q^T is the pricing measure with the zero-coupon bond P(·,T) as numéraire. Its defining property is that the forward price is the Q^T-expectation of the spot: E^{Q^T}[S_T] = S_0/P(0,T) = S_0·e^{rT} = F(0,T), the no-arbitrage forward price. theorems.name: Bootstrapping a Par Swap Recovers the Coupon-Bond Discount Factor
theorems.description: A payer swap with floating leg P0 − x (spot-starting when P0 = 1), fixed rate K and one fixed payment of K·δ at each date of the schedule and at the new maturity has zero value exactly when the coupon bond paying K·δ at those dates and face 1 at the last prices at P0 (the coupon-bond pricing equation of the closed-form bootstrap). If the new discount factor x solves that equation and 1 + K·δ > 0, bisection on the zero-quote swap from any bracket [lo, hi] containing x lands within (hi − lo)/2^{n+1} of x after n steps. The bracket containing x is a hypothesis; the rest of the curve (the earlier discount factors P) is taken as given.

/-- **Bootstrapping a par swap recovers the coupon-bond discount factor.** A zero-value
last-coupon swap at fixed rate `K` is the par coupon bond with coupon `K·δ` and face `1`; when
the new factor `x` solves that bond's pricing equation, bisection on the swap from a bracket
containing `x` lands within `(hi − lo)/2^{n+1}` of it. Re-exports
`MathFin.Bootstrapping.payerSwapValue_lastCoupon_eq_zero_iff_couponBond` and

    (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc lo hi) (n : ℕ) :

theorems.name: Vasicek Zero Yield in Nelson–Siegel Slope Factors
theorems.description: For the Vasicek short rate (κ > 0) and maturity T > 0, the continuously compounded zero yield −log P(0,T)/T of the bond price P(0,T) = E[exp(−∫₀ᵀ r_s ds)] equals (θ − σ²/(2κ²)) + (r₀ − θ + σ²/κ²)·s(κT) − (σ²/(2κ²))·s(2κT), where s(x) = (1 − e^{−x})/x is the Nelson–Siegel slope factor. So the Vasicek curve is a level plus slope factors at the two decay rates κ and 2κ. The expectation is under the measure carrying the Brownian driver, and the integrated rate is in its Wiener representation, as in the Vasicek bond-price entry.

theorems.name: Short and Long Ends of the Vasicek Yield Curve
theorems.description: For the Vasicek short rate with κ > 0, the continuously compounded zero yield −log P(0,T)/T of the bond price P(0,T) = E[exp(−∫₀ᵀ r_s ds)] tends to the initial short rate r₀ as T → 0⁺ and to the long rate θ − σ²/(2κ²) as T → ∞. Both limits are read off the Nelson–Siegel form of the Vasicek yield, using s(x) → 1 as x → 0 and s(x) → 0 as x → ∞ for the slope factor s(x) = (1 − e^{−x})/x. The expectation is under the measure carrying the Brownian driver, and the integrated rate is in its Wiener representation.

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter Topology
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- **The two ends of the Vasicek yield curve.** For `κ > 0`, the zero yield
`−log P(0,T)/T` tends to `r₀` as `T → 0⁺` and to `θ − σ²/(2κ²)` as `T → ∞`. Re-exports
`MathFin.tendsto_vasicekYield_nhdsGT_zero` and `MathFin.tendsto_vasicekYield_atTop`. -/
theorem vasicek_yield_curve_ends

    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (r₀ θ σ : ℝ) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) :
    Tendsto (fun T : ℝ≥0 ↦
        -Real.log (∫ ω, Real.exp (-(vasicekIntegratedRate hB r₀ θ σ hκ T ω)) ∂μ) / T)
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 r₀) ∧
    Tendsto (fun T : ℝ≥0 ↦
        -Real.log (∫ ω, Real.exp (-(vasicekIntegratedRate hB r₀ θ σ hκ T ω)) ∂μ) / T)
      atTop (𝓝 (θ - σ ^ 2 / (2 * κ ^ 2))) :=
  ⟨tendsto_vasicekYield_nhdsGT_zero hB r₀ θ σ hκ, tendsto_vasicekYield_atTop hB r₀ θ σ hκ⟩

theorems.name: ABCD Stochastic Integral Is Gaussian with the ABCD Total Variance
theorems.description: For the ABCD instantaneous volatility f(τ) = (a + bτ)e^{−cτ} + d with c ≠ 0, the Wiener integral ∫₀ᵀ f(T − u) dB_u of the deterministic integrand u ↦ f(T − u) against a pre-Brownian motion is centred Gaussian with variance v(T) = ∫₀ᵀ f(τ)² dτ, given by the closed-form antiderivative of the ABCD module. This is the log-forward noise of a forward rate with ABCD volatility.

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.WienerIntegralL2

/-- **The ABCD stochastic integral is Gaussian with the ABCD total variance.** For `c ≠ 0`,
`∫₀ᵀ f(T − u) dB_u ~ N(0, v(T))` with `v(T) = ∫₀ᵀ f²` in closed form. Re-exports
`MathFin.abcdWienerIntegral_hasLaw`. -/
theorem abcd_wiener_integral_gaussian
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (a b c d : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    HasLaw (fun ω ↦ wienerIntegralLp B hB T (abcdKernelLp a b c d T) ω)
      (gaussianReal 0 (abcdTotalVar a b c d T).toNNReal) μ :=
  abcdWienerIntegral_hasLaw hB a b c d hc T

theorems.name: Black-76 Price of a Lognormal Forward with ABCD Volatility
theorems.description: Take a driftless lognormal forward with ABCD instantaneous volatility f(T − u) at calendar time u, in solved form F_T = F₀·exp(−v(T)/2 + ∫₀ᵀ f(T − u) dB_u), with v(T) = ∫₀ᵀ f(τ)² dτ. For F₀, K, T > 0, c ≠ 0 and v(T) > 0, the e^{−rT}-discounted call E[e^{−rT}(F_T − K)⁺] equals the Black-76 price e^{−rT}(F₀Φ(d₁) − KΦ(d₂)) at the root-mean-square volatility √(v(T)/T). The forward's SDE is cited, not proved (the forward is taken in solved form), the expectation is under the measure carrying the Brownian motion (no change to the forward measure is built), and a caplet's accrual factor and payment-date discount factor are not modelled.

    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) {F₀ K : ℝ} (r a b c d : ℝ)

theorems.name: Riccati Loadings Make exp(A − B·r) Solve the Term-Structure PDE
theorems.description: For the one-factor affine short rate dr = κ(θ − r)dt + √(α + βr) dW: if loadings A and B satisfy the Riccati equations A'(τ) = −κθB(τ) + ½αB(τ)² and B'(τ) = 1 − κB(τ) − ½βB(τ)² at τ, then u(τ, r) = exp(A(τ) − B(τ)·r) satisfies the term-structure PDE −∂_τu + κ(θ − r)∂_ru + ½(α + βr)∂²_ru − r·u = 0 at (τ, r), with τ the time to maturity. Only this direction is proved: the entry does not show that u is the bond price E[exp(−∫r)], and no solution of the Riccati system is constructed here.

import MathFin.FixedIncome.AffineTermStructurePDE

open MathFin

/-- **The Riccati system implies the term-structure PDE** (one-factor affine models). If
`A' = −κθB + ½αB²` and `B' = 1 − κB − ½βB²` at `τ`, then `u = exp(A − B·r)` satisfies
`−∂_τu + κ(θ − r)∂_ru + ½(α + βr)∂²_ru − r·u = 0` at `(τ, r)`. Re-exports
`MathFin.affineBondPrice_solves_pde`. -/
theorem affine_bond_price_solves_term_structure_pde {κ θ α β : ℝ} {A B : ℝ → ℝ} {τ : ℝ}
    (hA : HasDerivAt A (-(κ * θ) * B τ + α / 2 * B τ ^ 2) τ)
    (hB : HasDerivAt B (1 - κ * B τ - β / 2 * B τ ^ 2) τ) (r : ℝ) :
    -deriv (fun t ↦ Real.exp (A t - B t * r)) τ
      + κ * (θ - r) * deriv (fun x ↦ Real.exp (A τ - B τ * x)) r
      + (α + β * r) / 2 * deriv (deriv fun x ↦ Real.exp (A τ - B τ * x)) r
      - r * Real.exp (A τ - B τ * r) = 0 :=
  affineBondPrice_solves_pde hA hB r

theorems.name: CIR Closed-Form Bond Price Solves the CIR Term-Structure PDE

theorems.name: Par Swap Rate Is Convex in the Final Discount Factor
theorems.description: Fix a swap schedule s, accrual δ > 0, the floating-leg start value P0 and every discount factor except the one at a payment date n ∈ s, with the remaining factors summing to C > 0 and P0 + C ≥ 0. Then the par swap rate (P0 − x)/(δ·(C + x)) of the curve whose factor at n is set to x is a convex function of x on [0, ∞). This convexity is the source of the CMS convexity adjustment; the adjustment itself is not derived.

import MathFin.FixedIncome.CMS

open MathFin MathFin.CMS

/-- **The par swap rate is convex in the final discount factor.** With every other discount
factor fixed (summing to `C > 0`, `P0 + C ≥ 0`) and `δ > 0`, the par rate of the curve updated
to `x` at `n ∈ s` is convex in `x ≥ 0`. Re-exports `MathFin.CMS.parSwapRate_update_eq` and
`MathFin.CMS.cmsCurveRate_convexOn`. -/
theorem par_swap_rate_convex_in_final_discount_factor {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (P0 δ : ℝ) (P : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι) {n : ι} (hn : n ∈ s) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hC : 0 < ∑ i ∈ s.erase n, P i) (hPC : 0 ≤ P0 + ∑ i ∈ s.erase n, P i) :
    ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Ici 0) (fun x ↦
      parSwapRate P0 (Function.update P n x n) (annuity δ (Function.update P n x) s)) := by
  rw [show (fun x ↦ parSwapRate P0 (Function.update P n x n)
      (annuity δ (Function.update P n x) s)) = cmsCurveRate P0 δ (∑ i ∈ s.erase n, P i) from
    funext fun x ↦ parSwapRate_update_eq P0 δ x P s hn]
  exact cmsCurveRate_convexOn P0 δ _ hδ hC hPC

theorems.name: Compact-Range Static Replication of the CMS Par-Rate Functional
theorems.description: For δ > 0 and a strike range [L, U] with L > −C, the par-rate functional S(x) = (P0 − x)/(δ·(C + x)) in the final discount factor x is replicated on [L, U] by cash S(κ), a forward position S'(κ)·(x − κ) and static strips of puts below κ and calls above κ on x with weights S''(K) = 2(P0 + C)/(δ(C + K)³): the Carr–Madan spanning identity restricted to a compact strike range. The unbounded-strike replication and the CMS convexity adjustment are not formalized.

open MathFin MathFin.CMS

/-- **Compact-range static replication of the CMS par-rate functional.** On `[L, U]` with
`L > −C`, `S(x) = S(κ) + S'(κ)(x − κ) + ∫_L^κ S''(K)(K − x)⁺ dK + ∫_κ^U S''(K)(x − K)⁺ dK`
for `S = cmsCurveRate P0 δ C`. Re-exports `MathFin.CMS.cmsCurveRate_spanning`. -/
theorem cms_par_rate_compact_spanning (P0 δ C : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    {L U κ S : ℝ} (hL : -C < L) (hLκ : L ≤ κ) (hκU : κ ≤ U) (hS : S ∈ Set.Icc L U) :
    cmsCurveRate P0 δ C S = cmsCurveRate P0 δ C κ
      + (-(P0 + C) / (δ * (C + κ) ^ 2)) * (S - κ)
      + (∫ K in L..κ, (2 * (P0 + C) / (δ * (C + K) ^ 3)) * max (K - S) 0)
      + (∫ K in κ..U, (2 * (P0 + C) / (δ * (C + K) ^ 3)) * max (S - K) 0) :=
  cmsCurveRate_spanning P0 δ C hδ hL hLκ hκU hS
